newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech leader Havel leaves for Belgian honeymoon.
newsitem.headline: Czech leader Havel leaves for Belgian honeymoon.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel left for a one-week honeymoon in Belgium on Friday, his first trip outside Prague since surgery to remove a cancerous lung tumour in December, his spokesman said.
Havel and his new wife, former actress Dagmar Veskrnova, 43, will spend a week at a health resort in Spa, Belgium.
After the trip Havel will return to normal duties at Prague Castle with the official visit of Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov scheduled for February 28.
Since leaving hospital, Havel, aged 60, has been recovering in his private villa in west Prague, working on official business only occasionally.
Havel surprised his fellow citizens when he married Veskrnova, now known in the Czech feminine as Havlova, in a secret ceremony on January 4 soon after his release from hospital.

The new first lady, who is well known to Czechs for her roles in numerous films, television programmes, and plays, gave her final performance as Queen Kristina at Prague's Vinohrady Theatre on Wednesday, then announced her retirement.
The former chain-smoking playwright Havel, who helped lead Prague's non-violent "Velvet Revolution" over communism in 1989, had half his right lung removed in the surgery on December 2.
Doctors have since said that his recovery required no further radical treatment.
Havel's first wife Olga died of cancer, aged 62, in January, 1996. The couple had no children together.
